activity.notes: Ur-Nammu was the founder and first ruler of the Third Dynasty of Ur. Museum records conventionally place his reign at 2112-2095 BCE and contemporary royal inscriptions style him King of Ur and King of Sumer and Akkad. ATLAS uses that conventional Middle-Chronology-scale interval for the year-level reign representation, but both absolute endpoints are marked approximate because third-millennium BCE Mesopotamian absolute chronology is reconstructed and alternative chronological schemes exist. The user-supplied label 'Ur III Dynasty' is normalized to the standard historical polity name Third Dynasty of Ur rather than treated as a separate identity.

sources.title: Ur-Nammu — British Museum Collections Online
sources.citation_text: The British Museum identifies Ur-Nammu as a Mesopotamian ruler of the Third Dynasty of Ur and gives his rule as 2112-2095 BCE.

sources.title: Inscribed brick — The Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.citation_text: The Metropolitan Museum dates the Ur III ruler Ur-Nammu to ca. 2112-2095 BCE and preserves an inscription naming him king of Ur and king of Sumer and Akkad.

sources.title: The Third Dynasty of Ur. The Stela of Ur-Nammu — Penn Museum Bulletin
sources.citation_text: The Penn Museum publication identifies Ur-Nammu as the founder of the Third Dynasty of Ur and describes the dynasty's kingship over Sumer and Akkad.
